text: True or False: Silicon nitride (Si3N4) waveguides suffer from strong two-photon absorption at 1550 nm, which limits their use in high-power applications.
explanation: False. Si3N4 has a large ~5 eV bandgap and therefore shows no two-photon absorption at 1550 nm, which, together with ultra-low loss down to 0.001 dB/cm, is exactly why it excels at high-power tasks like Kerr frequency combs. It is silicon, not silicon nitride, that suffers two-photon absorption above ~10 mW.
